sections.title: The Resurrection of Jesus
observations: This section describes the pivotal event of the resurrection, which is the cornerstone of Christian faith. The women arriving at the tomb find it empty, and an angel announces that Jesus has risen. This moment signifies victory over sin and death, fulfilling Jesus' own predictions about His resurrection.
The empty tomb is not just a miraculous event; it serves as a powerful testimony to the truth of Jesus' claims and the hope of eternal life for believers.

sections.title: The Great Commission
observations: After His resurrection, Jesus appears to His disciples and gives them the Great Commission, instructing them to make disciples of all nations. This command emphasizes the universal scope of the Gospel and the responsibility of believers to share their faith.
The promise of Jesus' presence 'to the end of the age' reassures believers of His continual support and guidance as they fulfill this mission.

importantVerses.commentary: He is not here; for He is risen, as He said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.
Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

questions: What does the resurrection of Jesus mean for the believer's faith and hope?
How does the Great Commission shape the mission of the church today?
In what ways can we practically fulfill the command to make disciples of all nations?
